title: Why Does Krishna Wear a Peacock Feather?

source.name: Traditional Krishna/Vrindavan story
source.episode_or_reference: Story idea supplied in stories/story_ideas.md; traditional account/folklore treatment, not presented as a direct scripture quotation.

characters.description: Warm Indian grandfather in his late 60s, white kurta-pajama, simple shawl, expressive kind face.
Indian girl aged about 8 in simple Indian clothes, curious expressive face.
Indian boy aged about 10 in simple Indian clothes, curious expressive face.

Bal Krishna, approximately 6–8 years old, unmistakably Shyam-varna with deep rich blue skin visible across face, neck, arms and hands; small pre-adolescent child proportions, never an adult or teenager. Soft round childlike face, large expressive dark eyes, short dark curly hair, peacock-feather crown, yellow pitambar, simple traditional gold jewelry. Fixed Krishna character identity: deep blue Shyam-varna skin must remain clearly visible in every generated reference and scene.

locations.description: Peaceful Vrindavan village courtyard beneath a huge old banyan tree, exposed roots, soft afternoon light, earthen ground, clay pots, village greenery and a calm storytelling atmosphere.
Beautiful Vrindavan grove with kadamba trees, wildflowers, soft breeze and peacocks in the distance.

supporting_assets.description: Indian peacock with natural blue-green plumage and detailed tail feathers.
Single elegant peacock feather used as Krishna's crown ornament.
